Isolated inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Defined as a scrotal reproductive-system neoplasm; no specific cutaneous or vascular origin established for the umbrella concept.
Tubular histidine transport defect; brain atrophy/ID and hearing loss 80-99%; skeletal and nail abnormalities also 80-99%, omitted by cap.
Benign tumour of vulvar vestibular glands, a reproductive site; unrelated to the ear's vestibular apparatus.
Mitochondrial energy-metabolism disease; neurologic impairment and skeletal myopathy each affect >30% across the group; other organ damage varies by subtype.
Inherited red-cell aplasia; cleft palate/lip 30-79% and thumb abnormalities 8/20; atrial septal defect 3/20 does not meet threshold.
Porphyrin metabolism defect; low penetrance limits neuropathy across all patients, cutaneous disease is usually <30%, and severe haemolysis belongs to rare biallelic forms.
Molybdenum cofactor deficiency causes defining severe encephalopathy, seizures and developmental impairment; brain malformations are documented.
Retinopathy, obesity/hypogonadism and polydactyly define BBS; renal structural or functional disease is a major diagnostic criterion, although subtype frequency is uncertain.
Porokeratosis with persistent keratotic lesions of palms, soles and other skin; no qualifying extracutaneous involvement.
Clonal dendritic-cell neoplasm; osteolysis 80-99%, infiltrative dermatitis and hepatic enlargement 30-79%; pulmonary and pituitary disease <30%.
Squamous carcinoma arising in the urethra, which belongs to the urinary axis.
Obstetric placental dysfunction; associated maternal autoimmune diseases and separately diagnosed offspring neurodevelopmental disorders do not add axes.
HIV-associated syndrome defined by muscle wasting with myofiber degeneration; malabsorption reflects intestinal dysfunction in 30-79%.
Inherited deficiency anaemias; metabolic, intestinal and hepatic abnormalities are subtype-specific rather than shared across the umbrella.
Inherited immunoglobulin D deficiency concerns humoral immunity; no evidence supports blood-cell disease or other organ damage.
Navicular osteonecrosis with bone collapse, deformity and secondary joint changes; vascular necrosis of bone does not establish systemic vascular disease.
Chorioretinal degeneration, hypopituitarism and hair abnormalities define the syndrome; ID/ataxia 30-79% and axonal neuropathy 3/7 support neurologic involvement.
Interstitial mesenchymal tumour arising in fetal or neonatal lung.
Defined neurologic disorder with recurrent nocturnal hemiplegic attacks; persistent developmental impairment is explicitly absent.
Thyroid peroxidase deficiency impairs thyroid hormone synthesis, causing congenital hypothyroidism and goitre; no qualifying additional organ damage established.
Benign or malignant neoplasm originating in skeletal muscle.
AGPS plasmalogen deficiency typically produces RCDP3; skeletal dysplasia, congenital cataracts and neurodevelopmental impairment occur in most (>80%) classic cases.
